transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I… I came because since my grandson was killed, something in me feels shut off. My daughter can sit right next to me holding my hand, and I know I love her… but I can’t feel the warmth of it inside.
Since your grandson passed away, have you found that you no longer enjoy things that you used to, like hobbies or spending time with family?
Yes… I suppose so. Being with my family, even my daughter sitting right there holding my hand… I know I love her, but I just don’t feel that warmth inside anymore. It’s like it’s gone quiet.
How long has it been since you started feeling this way?
About six days… since he was killed outside the community center. It started then.
Have you felt this way every day since your grandson passed away, or have there been days when you felt somewhat better?
Every day… yes. Since that day outside the community center. It’s been six days now, and it hasn’t really lifted.
Have you noticed that you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, or that you can’t enjoy things that used to bring you pleasure?
Yes… I can’t seem to feel much of anything good. My daughter can sit right beside me, holding my hand, and I know I love her… but I don’t feel the warmth of it inside. It’s just not there.
Have you also noticed that you feel down or hopeless during most of the day, nearly every day, or that you can't take pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Yes… I can’t really take pleasure in much. Since my grandson was killed, even when my daughter sits with me and holds my hand, I know I love her, but I can’t feel that warmth inside. It’s just… gone.
Besides feeling down and not enjoying things, have you experienced any other changes, like trouble sleeping, feeling tired all the time, or having trouble concentrating?
I… I don’t really know how to sort all that out. I haven’t been keeping track. Things just feel… heavy, I suppose.
Do you find yourself feeling numb or detached from people or activities that used to matter to you?
Yes… I do. Since my grandson was killed, it’s like something in me went quiet. My daughter can be right there holding my hand, and I know I love her… but I can’t feel the warmth of it. Not really.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just when you're reminded of your grandson?
I’m… not sure. It’s hard to separate it like that. It feels heavy a lot, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s most of the day every day, apart from… thinking about him.
Do you feel down or depressed even when you’re not thinking about your grandson?
I don’t know… I’m not sure I can tell the difference anymore. It all seems tied up with him, one way or another.
Can you describe what your mood feels like when you’re not actively thinking about your grandson? Do you still feel down or emotionally heavy during those moments?

I… I don’t really know how to tell. If I’m not thinking of him right that second, there’s still this sort of… dullness, I suppose. But I can’t say if it’s separate from all of that. It all feels mixed together.
Have you lost interest in doing things you used to care about, even things that didn’t have anything to do with your grandson?
I don’t know. I haven’t really… paid attention to it that way. I still do some things, I suppose, but it’s hard to say what I care about right now.
When you’re not thinking about your grandson, do you still feel a sense of sadness or emptiness inside?
I’m not sure. Maybe there’s something there… sort of hollow, but I can’t really separate it out like that.
Have you noticed that even activities you used to enjoy—like reading, watching TV, or being outside—don’t bring you any pleasure anymore, even when you’re not thinking about your grandson?
Yes… I think so. Even when my daughter sits right next to me, holding my hand… I know I love her, but I can’t seem to feel that warmth inside. It’s just… not there.

Can you think of any moment in the past week, even small things like having a cup of tea, hearing a bird sing, or seeing something beautiful, where you felt even a little bit of pleasure or joy inside?
No… I can’t think of one. Even with my daughter right there holding my hand, I know I love her, but I don’t feel that warmth inside. It’s just… not there.
Can you think of any activity, even something small or routine, that you’ve been able to enjoy even a little bit in the past six days?
No… I don’t think so. Since my grandson was killed, even with my daughter sitting right there holding my hand… I know I love her, but I can’t feel any warmth from it. Nothing really feels good.
Can you think of any activity, even something small or routine, that you’ve been able to enjoy even a little bit in the past six days, unrelated to thinking about your grandson?
No… not really. I’ve tried to just sit with my daughter, let her hold my hand, and I know I love her… but I don’t feel any of the warmth from it. Nothing comes through.
